note: Live capture: story_retrieve(project='browser-verification-test', entity_type='plot', fields=['all'], sections=['all']). Captured 2026-10-01 against the INSTALLED plugin after the four commits (dfeaf42, 5e17811, 8eaaf3c) and a full re-import. This is the capture that shows the fix: fields=['all'] now returns the five role fields, so a full plot retrieve shows its scenes.
before: fields=['all'] filtered out computed fields, so a full retrieve returned name, type, scope, value_arc, characters and five prose sections — and not one scene. The five role fields are the entire content of a plot entity.
findings: THE FIX, visible here: setups/crisis/climax/complications/resolutions are all present in `fields`. Before this they were absent from a ['all'] retrieve and had to be named one by one.
setups holds TWO entries for the-resistance — central-room-day and garden-dream. The multi-scene-per-role case, on live data, in the reader the agent actually uses.

An unfulfilled role appears TWICE, which is the point: `complications` is `[]` in `fields` AND the string 'complications' is in `unfilled_fields` for the-scientists-last-stand. Before, an unfilled role was invisible in both places — the fields were excluded from ['all'] and unfilled_fields skipped every computed field — so a plot with no crisis looked identical to a fully built one.

The-resistance has all five roles filled, so none of them is in its unfilled_fields. The only gaps it reports are genuine authoring gaps: one_sentence (a column, so unfilled_fields cannot see it — a false gap, pre-existing) and plot_type (genuinely unset).

CONFIRMED FALSE GAP, unchanged and still open: `one_sentence` is returned with a real value in `fields` and simultaneously listed in `unfilled_fields` on BOTH plots. It is a DB column, not an `extra` key, so the unfilled check cannot see it. This is the same blind spot that reports `location` on scenes, and it is why a plot looks like it is missing its logline when it has one.
the-scientists-last-stand reports `complications` — a REAL gap, deliberately left empty so the unfilled case is exercised by live data rather than only by a test.
the-core-day appears in the-scientists-last-stand twice, as climax AND resolution, matching the scene side. Two readers, one set of rows, no disagreement.
The two readers agree completely: every (plot, role, scene) triple in this payload appears in live_story_load_dramatic_elements_v2.json, and vice versa.

climax.description: Kael chooses to leave — not because the system is wrong, but because staying is.

complications.description: Kael returns to the Garden, but something has changed.

resolutions.description: The children emerge into the real world for the first time.

crisis.description: The Administrator makes its final offer. Kael refuses.

fields.one_sentence: Kael and Mira organize the children to breach the Central Room.

setups.description: Kael discovers the door isn't locked — it was never locked.
The spirals in the Garden dream are wrong. Kael cannot say why.

fields.name: The Resistance

sections.Summary: Kael's growing awareness of the system's wrongness becomes a quiet revolution. What begins as private questions becomes shared doubt, and shared doubt becomes organized resistance. The children must decide: accept the world as it is, or risk everything to find what's beyond the door.
sections.Threads:
- The Administrator controls every system — meals, light, access. Resistance means going without.
- Not all children want to leave. Some prefer the certainty of the known to the terror of the unknown.
- Kael's own doubt: what if the wrongness is in them, not the system?
sections.Value: If they fail, the children remain in a dying system — safe but stagnant, alive but not living. If they succeed, they step into a world that was never designed for them, with no guarantee of survival. The door opens both ways.

climax.description: The last scientist seals the door from the inside — the ultimate sacrifice that becomes the children's prison.

resolutions.description: The door is sealed. The children will wake 400 years later with no idea what was done to save them.

crisis.description: Dr. Voss argues with Marcus about whether to wake the children or let them sleep forever.

fields.one_sentence: 400 years earlier, the scientists race to complete Project Save the Children as the outsiders gather.

setups.description: The scientists first realize the Institute is failing — and the children are the only survivors.

fields.name: The Scientists' Last Stand

sections.Summary: Dr. Elena Voss and her team built the Institute to save the last children of a dying world. But 400 years later, their sanctuary has become a prison — and the children they saved are now trying to escape. The scientists' sacrifice is the reason the Institute exists; their failure is the reason it's dying.
sections.Threads:
- The Institute's power systems are failing. There's not enough energy to keep the children alive and the doors sealed.
- Marcus wants to wake the children. Elena believes the world outside is still uninhabitable.
- The outsiders are at the gates. The scientists must choose: open the door to save the children, or seal it to protect them.
sections.Value: If the scientists succeed, the children survive — but in a cage. If they fail, the Institute collapses and everyone dies. Either way, the children will never see the sky.
